text:
maria (oncall): heads up — multiple customers in na-west reporting streams that go 'silent' for 1-5s and then clients immediately reconnect. seeing a big customer impact and support escalations :rotating_light:
support-ops: customer ticket excerpts: 'stream drops mid-response, client reconnects and gets duplicate partial outputs', some report 502 then empty frames. forwarded logs attached.
sam (eng-sre): ack — are these full TCP disconnects or just empty SSE chunks? can you paste a raw client wire log?
support-ops: pasted sample (trimmed):
```
GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-8 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
...
--- then client gets
data:

event: keepalive

(then nothing for 2.1s)

connection reset by peer
```
ks: customers show rapid reconnect attempts after the silence.
kyung (infra): prometheus shows high downstream queue length on fanout nodes in na-west around 03:12–03:18 UTC, and a correlating spike in `sse_disconnects_total`. could be an internal backpressure causing streams to stall.
devops-bot: ALERT: na-west sse_disconnect_rate > 5x baseline (3m avg) — incident auto-opened.
sam (eng-sre): hypothesis: fanout worker overloaded -> stops emitting chunk frames for some sessions (zero-length/no-op), clients treat as stall and reconnect. We should confirm whether our keepalive/heartbeat handling is dropping on the fanout path.
lee (platform): looking at fanout logs now — I see sequences like `emit_chunk()` succeeded but consumer ack delayed ~2s, then `stream_write()` returns EAGAIN and we mark session as stalled. Might be a select/poll starvation under high epoll loop latency.
kyung (infra): repro steps I ran from a test client (na-west):
```
# repro quick script
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" "https://api.na-west.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=..." 
# observe: initial data, then silent period ~2s, then server closes socket
```
support-ops: customer impact list (redacted): 5 accounts with webapps showing partial UI renders and automatic reconnection loops. support is getting billing complaints — they think they got billed twice for partial outputs.
sam (eng-sre): immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase keepalive frequency on the edge for na-west to avoid client reconnect storms, 2) route new sessions to eu-west as a failover for affected customers, 3) push a short-lived server change to treat short zero-byte frames as no-op rather than stall. which ones can we do quickly?
lee (platform): can do (2) via routing rule change in ~8–12m (canary then full for na-west), and (1) edge keepalive tweak can be rolled in ~5m (config only). (3) needs a small runtime patch — I can prepare a canary build but will take ~30–40m to run through canary.
maria (oncall): please do (1) and (2) now. I’ll update status page & notify support. @support-ops please send customer comms template.
support-ops: posting template now:
"We’re investigating an issue affecting streaming sessions in na-west that may cause brief interruptions and reconnects. We recommend switching to the eu-west endpoint as a temporary workaround. We're prioritizing a fix and will follow up with timelines"
deploy-bot: edge-config-change: keepalive-interval=10s deployed to na-west-edge (canary) — OK
lee (platform): routing change to failover sessions -> eu-west started (canary 5% -> 50% now). monitor logs.
kyung (infra): fanout queue drain improved after routing shift; `sse_disconnects_total` dropped to ~1.2x baseline in the canary shards. good sign.
sam (eng-sre): for billing — we need to mark reconnect storms as non-chargeable duplicates for affected sessions window. tagging billing team and creating a ticket. note: avoid auto-refunding tokens until we confirm dedupe safety.
support-ops: created billing ticket #BILL-4621, assigned to finance. customer-facing note queued.
maria (oncall): status page update posted: "Partial streaming interruptions in na-west — failover & mitigations in progress. Some customers may see automatic reconnection. Workarounds: use eu-west endpoint or switch to polling mode temporarily."
sam (eng-sre): root cause plan: 1) collect fanout worker epoll latency traces, 2) add backpressure metrics per-session, 3) adjust runtime to tolerate short EAGAINs (treat as transient, not terminal), 4) add server-side short-heartbeat frames to reduce client-driven reconnects.
lee (platform): I have a canary runtime patch ready that softens the stall detection and treats zero-length frames as heartbeat; will canary it to 10% traffic in 30m if no regressions.
deploy-bot: runtime-canary: sse-heartbeat-tolerance v2026.3.15-rc1 -> canary 10% started
support-ops: customers updated; a few reported immediate improvement after being routed to eu-west.
kyung (infra): adding an alert to avoid future silent-chunk storms: alert if `sse_last_chunk_age` > 1s for >1% of sessions over 3m.
maria (oncall): good work. post-incident actions: schedule infra postmortem, update SDK docs w/ reconnection best practices and default backoff, confirm billing dedupe, and follow up with customers whose UX was impacted. tagging owners: @sam (eng-sre) for root cause & fix, @lee (platform) for rollout plan, @kyung (infra) for monitoring + alerts, @support-ops for comms & billing.
sam (eng-sre): will open a follow-up doc with traces and timeline. tentative RCA: fanout epoll latency + aggressive client reconnect heuristics -> silent-chunk storm -> reconnect loops -> perceived duplicate billing and partial outputs.
maria (oncall): incident status: mitigated (traffic failover + keepalive tweak). leaving this thread open for final RCA and billing confirmation. :white_check_mark:
